# MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?

> MindTopo is a benchmark of topological intuition for foundation models: the ability to perceive, infer, and operate on spatial relations that stay invariant under continuous deformation, such as connectivity, enclosure, and knottedness. It covers five properties grounded in cognitive science and formal topology (continuity, separation, order, enclosure, knots) at two cognitive levels, reasoning over rendered scenes and planning in interactive environments, with 13 procedurally generated task types and 3,900 evaluation instances split evenly between an Easy and a Hard level. Paper: "MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?" by Yunfei Ge, Anbang Liu, Qineng Wang, Johnalbert Garnica, Jianwen Lyu, Zihan Wang, Reuben Tan, Jianfeng Gao, Ruohan Zhang, Yining Hong, Jiajun Wu, and Manling Li (Northwestern University, Microsoft Research, Stanford University).

Key facts:
- Topological properties survive continuous deformation: a rope can be bent, stretched, or coiled, but whether it is knotted does not change.
- Five properties: continuity (is there an unbroken path?), separation (one whole or distinct parts?), order (what comes before what?), enclosure (inside or outside?), and knots (truly knotted or just tangled?).
- Two cognitive levels: reasoning (identify a topological relation in a rendered scene, or predict how it changes) and planning (act as a closed-loop agent in an interactive gym until a topological goal holds).
- Scale: 13 task types, 3,900 evaluation instances (2,400 reasoning questions, 1,500 planning episodes), 300 per task with 150 Easy and 150 Hard. The generators produce an 11,030-instance pool for the public release.
- Results: 13 MLLMs evaluated. Every model scores lower on planning than on reasoning. The best, GPT-6 Astra, averages 59.54% on reasoning and 49.80% on planning. On the Easy level, where humans were evaluated, it reaches 76.33% / 81.87% against 94.23% / 99.87% for humans. No open-weight model exceeds 1% average planning success (random legal actions: 0.53%).
- Training: on Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, SFT followed by RL lifts average reasoning accuracy from 14.24% to 51.53% but planning success only from 0.20% to 6.33%; gains on held-out tasks are uneven.
- Visual imagination: generated next-state images help where a local cue suffices (Sheep, 2D Maze) but not on trajectory-wide invariants (One Stroke). Six video generators reach a solved final frame in up to 35.2% of rollouts, yet 0 of 1,890 rollouts are process-valid. A manual audit of 119 Wan2.2-I2V-A14B rollouts found dynamics violations in 116.
